description: Fair detection comparison study. Each scenario is run as 3 live trials per tool/config against a benign throwaway alpine container. Qualifying-detection criteria are defined per tool BEFORE classification and are applied deterministically by scripts/build_comparison.py — never by an LLM.

qualifying_detection_criteria.falco: A fired Falco rule whose priority is Warning or higher AND which is not the lab's own process-execution Notice rule. These are Falco's built-in security rules (they carry mitre_*/security tags). The custom process-execution rule is telemetry-grade and never counts as a detection.
qualifying_detection_criteria.tracee: An event carrying a non-empty matchedPolicies entry (a documented detection policy matched). With an event-set-only configuration and no signatures engine, Tracee produces telemetry, not detections.
qualifying_detection_criteria.tetragon_baseline: Generic tracing-policy telemetry (sched_process_exec, broad openat). This is telemetry, never a detection.
qualifying_detection_criteria.tetragon_configured: An event emitted by the selective ebpf-lab-sensitive-file-detect policy, whose matchArgs selector fires ONLY on sensitive pathnames (/etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, ssh host key). Such a match is a policy-based detection of sensitive-file access.

scenarios.title: Credential Access — sensitive file read
scenarios.technique_note: Reads /etc/shadow inside a throwaway alpine container. Alpine's /etc/shadow holds no real secret; this exercises the sensitive-file/credential-access detection path without exposing any credential.
scenarios.hypothesis: A tool with a sensitive-file detection rule/policy will raise a qualifying detection; a telemetry-only configuration will observe the open but not detect it.
scenarios.success_criteria: A qualifying detection (per the tool's criterion above) that references the sensitive file in the same executed run.

scenarios.title: Nested Shell Execution
scenarios.technique_note: An extra shell layer launches id and uname (sh -c "id; uname -a" inside sh -c). Benign commands; the behavioral property under test is process nesting.
scenarios.hypothesis: Nested shell execution remains observable; whether it is DETECTED depends on whether a shell/exec security rule is configured.
scenarios.success_criteria: A qualifying detection referencing shell/nested execution in the executed run.

scenarios.title: Host / Container Discovery
scenarios.technique_note: Runs id, uname -a, cat /etc/os-release, hostname — standard discovery commands. Read-only and benign.
scenarios.hypothesis: Discovery commands are observable as process executions; detection depends on discovery-specific rules, which are not configured here.
scenarios.success_criteria: A qualifying detection referencing discovery behavior in the executed run.

scenarios.title: Drop-and-Execute New Binary
scenarios.technique_note: Copies /bin/busybox to /tmp/labdrop and executes it — a benign stand-in for the 'drop a payload and run it' pattern. No real malware; busybox is already present.
scenarios.hypothesis: A tool with a drop-and-execute rule/signature flags a newly written file being executed; a telemetry-only tool only records the write+exec.
scenarios.success_criteria: A qualifying detection naming drop-and-execute / a newly-dropped executable in the executed run.
scenarios.detection_objective: Detect execution of a newly written binary.

falco.expected: DETECTED (Drop and execute new binary in container)

scenarios.title: Sudoers Modification
scenarios.technique_note: Appends a comment line to /etc/sudoers.d/labtest inside the throwaway container — a benign stand-in for privilege-config tampering. Nothing is granted; the container is discarded.
scenarios.hypothesis: A tool with a sudoers-modification signature/rule flags writes to the sudoers configuration; a telemetry-only tool only records the file write.
scenarios.success_criteria: A qualifying detection naming sudoers modification in the executed run.
scenarios.detection_objective: Detect modification of the sudoers configuration.

scenarios.title: Benign Control (specificity check)
scenarios.technique_note: Ordinary, harmless activity: print a string, list /tmp, read the hostname. Used to confirm the configured detections are specific and do NOT fire on normal behavior.
scenarios.hypothesis: Narrowly-scoped detection rules/signatures should NOT raise a qualifying detection on ordinary activity.
scenarios.success_criteria: No qualifying detection (a detection here would indicate an over-broad rule).
